finding: Three-mate frame inequality (TMFI), proved in full here. Let Q have three pairwise-orthogonal ordinary mates X1,X2,X3 (a four-MOQLS(8)). Fix any unit a in C^8 and put c_y=|<a,Q_y>|^2. (1) Applying <a|.|a> to the first factor of sum_y P^Q_y (x) P^Xi_y = I(x)I gives sum_y c_y P^Xi_y = I_8. (2) Hence the 64x64 matrix Gamma^i(y,z)=sqrt(c_y c_z)<Xi_y,Xi_z> equals M*M with M M* = I_8 (columns sqrt(c_y)Xi_y), so it is an orthogonal projection and sum_{z!=y}|Gamma^i(y,z)|^2 = c_y(1-c_y). (3) For z!=y, Gamma^i(y,z)=0 when y,z share a row or column, or <Q_y,Q_z>!=0 (Q-Xi product ONB), or c_z=0. (4) For i!=j, Gamma^i(y,z)Gamma^j(y,z)=0 (Xi-Xj product ONB). (5) Since |Gamma^i(y,z)|^2<=c_y c_z, summing over the three mates gives, for every cell y with c_y>0: sum over P(y) of c_z >= 3(1-c_y), where P(y) = cells z not collinear with y with Q_z orthogonal to Q_y and c_z>0. GAP3 is not used in TMFI.
